title: Grandmommy’s Pecan Pie
status: Complete editorial review; implemented and production verified

exactBefore.body:
## Chef's Note

Southern pecan pie is built on a simple syrup custard that's meant to barely set - you're aiming for that wobbling center that firms up completely as it cools. Karo syrup is traditional for a reason: it creates the right balance of sweetness and texture without crystallizing. Don't skip the cooling step; this pie needs at least two hours to develop its proper structure.

## Directions

1.  **Prep:** Preheat oven to 350°F. Place the unbaked pie shells on a baking sheet.
2.  **The Mix:** In a large bowl, whisk together the sugar, Karo syrup, and slightly beaten eggs until well combined.
3.  **The Emulsion:** Slowly whisk in the melted butter, vanilla, and salt until the filling is glossy and uniform.
4.  **Layer:** Divide the pecans evenly between the two pie shells. Pour the syrup mixture over the pecans - they will naturally float to the top to create the Crunch layer.
5.  **Bake:** Bake for 40-45 minutes until the edges are set and the center has a slight, stable wobble (the Texture).
6.  **Cool:** Let cool completely (at least 2 hours) before slicing. This is mandatory for the structure to set.

frontmatter.title: Grandmommy’s Pecan Pie
frontmatter.totalTime: About 3–5 hr, including cooling and chilling
ingredients: 2 unbaked pastry pie shells, prepared and ready to fill; choose shells that can hold the filling below their rims
4 tbsp (1/2 stick) unsalted butter, melted and cooled until warm

ingredients.name: unbaked pastry pie shell

steps.title: Prepare the shells
steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Set {{ingredients}} on a rimmed baking sheet. Prepare or handle the pastry according to its dough recipe or package instructions; this route uses unbaked pastry shells. Leave enough space below the rims for the filling to move slightly during baking. For the original batch, each shell must hold half the complete filling; do not force a deep mound into a small shell.

steps.title: Mix the syrup filling
steps.text: Combine {{ingredients}} in the bowl in this order: stir the sugar and syrup together, then mix in the slightly beaten eggs until evenly blended.

steps.title: Add the melted fat and vanilla
steps.text: Stir in {{ingredients}} until uniform. The melted fat should be warm enough to remain liquid but not hot enough to cook the eggs.

steps.title: Stir in all the pecans
steps.text: Stir in {{ingredients}} last, keeping all the nuts and syrup mixture together.

steps.title: Divide the complete filling
steps.text: Share the whole nut-and-syrup mixture equally among the prepared shells, stirring between pours so each receives nuts as well as syrup. Check that the filling stays below the rims; if the chosen shells are too small, use larger shells rather than discarding filling.

steps.title: Bake until the filling is set
steps.text: Bake at 350°F, beginning the first check around 40 minutes. Continue until the edges are set and the center moves together with only a gentle tremble, rather than a liquid wave. A food thermometer placed in the central filling, away from a nut or the pan, must read at least 160°F; keep baking until the filling also has the set texture. Shield the pastry edges with foil if they brown too quickly. Shell depth, frozen pastry and oven heat can change the time, so check each pie separately and remove it when ready.

steps.title: Cool, then chill completely
steps.text: Set the baked pies on a rack until the initial steam subsides, then refrigerate them while still warm if necessary. Get them into the refrigerator within 2 hours of baking, or within 1 hour above 90°F. Leave them in the refrigerator until completely cool and firm before slicing; do not extend counter cooling to wait for a clean slice.

learning.focus: Bake the egg filling through, protect the pastry and chill before slicing.
learning.outcome: Set pecan filling in baked pastry, with a center that slices after full chilling.
before: Use the listed melted unsalted butter and sea-salt pinch. Stir all the pecans into the filling before dividing it among the shells.
Have unbaked pastry shells ready to fill. Choose shells that will hold the complete filling below their rims; the original batch uses two shells.
Scale the whole filling proportionally. A half batch uses one shell; choose batch sizes and shell sizes that give usable whole shells.
Make refrigerator space for all the pies so cooling does not require prolonged counter holding.

checkpoints.cue: The fat is liquid but only warm, and the filling is evenly mixed.
checkpoints.why: Very hot melted fat can cook small egg pieces before baking.

checkpoints.cue: All nuts and filling are divided among the shells below the rims.
checkpoints.why: Actual filling fit matters more than an assumed universal pie diameter.

checkpoints.cue: The center has no liquid wave and reaches at least 160°F in the filling.
checkpoints.why: Surface color and a loose wobble alone do not establish a cooked egg center.

troubleshooting.problem: The crust edges brown while the center remains loose.
troubleshooting.cause: The exposed pastry cooks more quickly than the egg filling.
troubleshooting.fix: Shield the edges with foil and keep baking at 350°F until the central filling is set and reaches at least 160°F.

troubleshooting.problem: The filling seems firm near the edge but flows at the middle.
troubleshooting.cause: The center has not finished cooking, or the pie has not chilled fully.
troubleshooting.fix: Confirm the central baking endpoint first, then refrigerate promptly and allow full chilling before slicing.

troubleshooting.problem: The filling will not fit the chosen shells.
troubleshooting.cause: The shells are too small or shallow for the batch.
troubleshooting.fix: Use larger unbaked pastry shells before filling; keep the same complete formula rather than throwing away nuts or syrup.

learning.storage: Refrigerate the baked pies at 40°F or below within 2 hours of baking, or within 1 hour above 90°F, while still warm if necessary. Cover after cooling and use within 3–4 days of baking. For longer storage, wrap cooled pies or slices airtight and freeze promptly at 0°F; 1–2 months is the FoodSafety.gov quality window for pecan pie. Thaw in the refrigerator. Keep leftovers refrigerated after slicing.
learning.timing: Allow about 15–20 minutes to mix and fill, and begin checking the bake around the source’s 40-minute point. A 40–60-minute bake is a planning range; shell depth and starting temperature may require longer. Allow roughly 2–4 hours for rack settling and refrigerator chilling, continuing until the filling is fully cool and firm. Move pies into refrigeration within the stated counter-time limit rather than waiting for full room-temperature cooling. Larger batches need extra shells and oven loads, not a multiplied bake time.

exactAfter.body:
## Chef's Note

Pecans, light corn syrup and vanilla make a rich filling that firms as it chills. Give the center time to set while protecting the pastry edges, then refrigerate promptly and let the pies cool completely before slicing.

## Directions

1. **Prepare the shells:** Heat the oven to 350°F. Set unbaked pastry pie shells on a rimmed baking sheet. Prepare or handle the pastry according to its dough recipe or package instructions; this route uses unbaked pastry shells. Leave enough space below the rims for the filling to move slightly during baking. For the original batch, each shell must hold half the complete filling; do not force a deep mound into a small shell.
2. **Mix the syrup filling:** Combine granulated sugar, light corn syrup, and large eggs in the bowl in this order: stir the sugar and syrup together, then mix in the slightly beaten eggs until evenly blended.
3. **Add the melted fat and vanilla:** Stir in unsalted butter, vanilla extract, and sea salt until uniform. The melted fat should be warm enough to remain liquid but not hot enough to cook the eggs.
4. **Stir in all the pecans:** Stir in pecan halves last, keeping all the nuts and syrup mixture together.
5. **Divide the complete filling:** Share the whole nut-and-syrup mixture equally among the prepared shells, stirring between pours so each receives nuts as well as syrup. Check that the filling stays below the rims; if the chosen shells are too small, use larger shells rather than discarding filling.
6. **Bake until the filling is set:** Bake at 350°F, beginning the first check around 40 minutes. Continue until the edges are set and the center moves together with only a gentle tremble, rather than a liquid wave. A food thermometer placed in the central filling, away from a nut or the pan, must read at least 160°F; keep baking until the filling also has the set texture. Shield the pastry edges with foil if they brown too quickly. Shell depth, frozen pastry and oven heat can change the time, so check each pie separately and remove it when ready.
7. **Cool, then chill completely:** Set the baked pies on a rack until the initial steam subsides, then refrigerate them while still warm if necessary. Get them into the refrigerator within 2 hours of baking, or within 1 hour above 90°F. Leave them in the refrigerator until completely cool and firm before slicing; do not extend counter cooling to wait for a clean slice.

sourceDifferences: Full current four-tablespoon unsalted butter equals half a conventional U.S. butter stick/2 ounces; no extra fat or formula reduction. Family half-margarine-stick is preserved only in the private original.

Four large eggs, pecan halves, unbaked shells and a sea-salt pinch are retained modern current choices; the original egg size, nut cut, shell state and no-added-salt formula are distinguished privately.
Native nuts stirred in last now inform this butter adaptation. All nuts and syrup are distributed equally among usable whole shells, with no active layered or margarine version.
Set texture plus FDA minimum 160°F, prompt refrigeration and full chilling replace unsafe loose-wobble/long-counter-cooling implications without adopting Karo’s different formula or quality endpoint.
